title: RAPTOR: Practical Numerical Profiling of Scientific Applications
problem: Modern HPC architectures proliferate low-precision units (FP16, FP32) while reducing FP64 capabilities, forcing scientists to evaluate code precision requirements. Traditional search-and-replace FP64→FP16 approaches fail; principled precision lowering requires guided analysis.
motivation: AI-driven hardware trends reduce FP64 support while introducing novel low-precision units. Scientists must re-evaluate numerical requirements but lack tools for systematic precision profiling. Numerical instabilities and accuracy loss are non-obvious when lowering precision.
method: LLVM-based numerical profiling tool (RAPTOR) that: (1) Transparently replaces high-precision computations with low-precision units, (2) Emulates user-defined precision formats, (3) Identifies code regions where precision lowering is feasible, (4) Profiles numerical stability and error propagation.
key_novelty: First LLVM-based tool for systematic numerical profiling across mixed-precision HPC codes. Enables guided precision lowering by identifying regions tolerant of low precision while detecting instabilities.
contributions: LLVM-based transparent precision replacement and emulation for profiling
Numerical stability analysis across low-precision formats
Practical workflow for evaluating precision requirements in scientific codes
Demonstration on four real-world multi-physics Flash-X applications
hardware_target: Modern HPC systems with low-precision units
limitations: Abstract-only; specific precision formats tested, accuracy tolerance thresholds, and performance improvement numbers not provided. Applicability to production workflows unclear.
primary_theme: Automated numerical precision profiling for heterogeneous hardware
